history.summary: An 8th-century Rashtrakuta monolithic rock-cut temple carved from a single basalt rock (built during the reign attributed to Krishna I). It has three rock-cut sanctums (likely originally Brahma-Shiva-Vishnu; now Ganesha-Shiva-Parvati), a cube-shaped garbhagriha housing the Shiva linga, and a distinctive circular Nandi mandapa. It was left unfinished - possibly due to a fault line discovered in the rock - which reveals ancient construction techniques. Folk legend credits the Pandavas. It is Pune's oldest monument, an ASI-protected national monument; the Peshwas donated for its upkeep and new idols (Parvati, Ganesha; modern Rama-Sita-Lakshmana marbles) were added in the 19th century.

name: Pataleshwar Cave Temple
town_description: The caves lie on Jangali Maharaj Road in Shivajinagar, in the heart of Pune city, on a rocky hillock west of the Mula-Mutha sangam; once outside the town, now fully surrounded by urban development.

travel.railway: Pune Junction, ~3-4 km southeast (12-20 min drive)
travel.road: Jangali Maharaj Road, Shivajinagar; no dedicated parking - use nearby paid parking on JM Road; entry free

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; mornings (avoid summer afternoons)
visitor_information.opening_hours: 8:30 AM to 5:30 PM daily (ASI monument hours; entry free). Opening-hour conflict: some listings report 8:00 AM to 8:00 PM (verify)
